result.title: CHARTER: Auditing Reference Substitution in Hierarchical Compact-Evidence Evaluation for Computational Pathology
result.summary: In digital pathology, compact evidence is often used to explain or audit predictions made by whole-slide image multiple instance learning models. In hierarchical compact-evidence pipelines, candidate filtering introduces a strategy-specific candidate-conditioned prediction alongside the original full-bag prediction. If the evaluation reference changes while the intended target remains the original full-bag prediction, however, not only can the measured fidelity of the same compact evidence change, but comparisons between competing candidate strategies can also change. To make this dependence explicit, we introduce CHARTER, a reference-aware evaluation charter that asks researchers to DECLARE the intended target and reference, QUANTIFY candidate-induced prediction shift, and AUDIT the stability of comparative conclusions. Across the 15 comparisons in our main five-seed Random-K audit, 4 showed determinate reversals; in a matched native-ranking stress test, the ACMIL comparison changed from REVERSED to PRESERVED. CHARTER turns otherwise implicit candidate-filtering and reference choices into an auditable evaluation specification, helping distinguish genuine preservation of the intended prediction from apparent gains induced by changing the prediction being explained.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对计算病理中的层次化紧凑证据评估，提出 CHARTER 评估章程：要求显式声明预期目标与参考、量化候选筛选引起的预测偏移，并审计比较结论的稳定性，发现多项对比会因参考变更而反转。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「候选筛选引入候选条件预测、参考替换改变忠实度与结论」的审计思路，可能启发 LVR 中对视觉证据筛选与「解释对象/参考基准」漂移的因果归因与评价设计。
